result.topic_en: Euler completes a descent proof that any divisor of a sum of four squares (with suitable conditions) is itself a sum of four squares, then gives the analogous descent proof that divisors of a sum of two coprime squares are sums of two squares, and begins a simpler alternative proof of the four-squares divisor theorem.
result.transcription:
$a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=nn'$, et quia $a<\frac{1}{2}n$, $b<\frac{1}{2}n$, $c<\frac{1}{2}n$, $d<\frac{1}{2}n$,
erit summa $a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2<n^2$, ideoque $nn'<n^2$, ergo $n'<n$,
nisi forte sit $n=1$. Divisa ergo per $n$ illa aequatione, prodit
$N=N^2n'+2NA+n(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2)$,
quae per $n'$ multiplicetur, ut habeamus
$Nn'=N^2n'^2+2Nn'A+nn'(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2)$;
quia autem $nn'=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2$, ultimum illud membrum abit in
$(a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2)(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2)=A^2+B^2+C^2+D^2$
per lemma II; consequenter
$Nn'=N^2n'^2+2Nn'A+A^2+B^2+C^2+D^2=(Nn'+A)^2+B^2+C^2+D^2$.
Sicque formula $Nn'$ etiam erit summa quatuor quadratorum, existente $n'<n$. Eodem modo pervenire licebit ad formas ulteriores $Nn''$, $Nn'''$ etc. ita, ut sit $n''<n'$, $n'''<n''$ etc. sicque tandem perveniri necesse est ad formam $N.1$, quae ergo etiam est summa quatuor quadratorum. Q. E. D.
Hinc etiam sequens Theorema facilius demonstrari potest, quam hactenus est factum:
Summa duorum quadratorum inter se primorum alios non admittit divisores, nisi qui ipsi sint summae duorum quadratorum.
Lemma. Productum ex duabus summis duorum quadratorum ipsum in duo quadrata resolvere.
Sit productum $(a^2+b^2)(\alpha^2+\beta^2)$, et sumtis $A=a\alpha+b\beta$ et $B=a\beta-b\alpha$, erit
$(a^2+b^2)(\alpha^2+\beta^2)=A^2+B^2$.
Si nunc $N$ fuerit divisor formae $p^2+q^2$, posito quoto $=n$, habetur $Nn=p^2+q^2$. Nunc igitur $p$ et $q$ ita exhibeantur, ut sit $p=Na+n\alpha$ et $q=Nb+n\beta$, ita, ut $a$ et $b$ sint minores quam $\frac{1}{2}n$; hincque $a^2+b^2<\frac{1}{2}n^2$,
quo substituto fit
$Nn=N^2(a^2+b^2)+2Nn(a\alpha+b\beta)+n^2(\alpha^2+\beta^2)$,
quae cum per $n$ divisibilis esse debeat, statuatur $a^2+b^2=nn'$, et diviso per $n$ erit
$N=N^2n'+2NA+n(\alpha^2+\beta^2)$.
Multiplicetur per $n'$, erit
$Nn'=N^2n'^2+2Nn'A+nn'(\alpha^2+\beta^2)$
at $nn'(\alpha^2+\beta^2)=A^2+B^2$, ergo
$Nn'=N^2n'^2+2Nn'A+A^2+B^2=(Nn'+A)^2+B^2$,
sicque $Nn'$ est etiam summa duorum quadratorum, ubi $n'<\frac{1}{2}n$. Hocque modo ulterius progrediendo mox pervenietur ad $N.1$. Consequenter $N$ certo erit summa duorum quadratorum.
Alia demonstratio simplicior ejusdem theorematis.
Si numerus quicunque $N$ fuerit divisor summae quatuor quadratorum $P^2+Q^2+R^2+S^2$, quae singula seorsim per eum non sint divisibilia, ille ipse numerus quoque erit summa quatuor quadratorum.
Demonstratio. I. Illa quadrata semper ad alia reduci possunt minora quam $\frac{1}{4}N^2$. Ponatur enim
$P=\mathfrak{A}N\mp p$, $Q=\mathfrak{B}N\mp q$, $R=\mathfrak{C}N\mp r$, $S=\mathfrak{D}N\mp s$,
ubi literae $\mathfrak{A}$, $\mathfrak{B}$, $\mathfrak{C}$, $\mathfrak{D}$ ita assumi possunt, ut numeri $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ infra semissem numeri $N$ deprimantur, quibus substitutis evidens est, formulam $p^2+q^2+r^2+s^2$, quae utique minor erit quam $N^2$, divisibilem fore per $N$ et quotum fore minorem quam $N$.
II. Sit ergo iste quotus $=n$, ut sit $Nn=p^2+q^2+r^2+s^2$, et ratione hujus numeri $n$ radices istorum quadratorum ita exhiberi poterunt
$p=a+\alpha n$, $q=b+\beta n$, $r=c+\gamma n$ et $s=d+\delta n$,

methods.what: Descent step for four squares: since remainders are below n/2, the new quotient n' is smaller than n
Four-square identity used to show Nn' is a sum of four squares

methods.quote: Eodem modo pervenire licebit ad formas ulteriores $Nn''$, $Nn'''$ etc. ita, ut sit $n''<n'$, $n'''<n''$ etc. sicque tandem perveniri necesse est ad formam $N.1$

methods.what: Descent proof that divisors of sums of two squares are sums of two squares
Reduction of roots modulo N to absolute values below N/2 (least absolute residues)
Writing roots relative to the quotient n

items.quote: Summa duorum quadratorum inter se primorum alios non admittit divisores, nisi qui ipsi sint summae duorum quadratorum.
items.english: A sum of two mutually prime squares admits no divisors other than those which are themselves sums of two squares.

items.quote: Productum ex duabus summis duorum quadratorum ipsum in duo quadrata resolvere.
items.english: To resolve the product of two sums of two squares itself into two squares.

items.quote: Si numerus quicunque $N$ fuerit divisor summae quatuor quadratorum $P^2+Q^2+R^2+S^2$, quae singula seorsim per eum non sint divisibilia, ille ipse numerus quoque erit summa quatuor quadratorum.
items.english: If any number N is a divisor of a sum of four squares P²+Q²+R²+S², which are not each separately divisible by it, that number is itself also a sum of four squares.
